redundancies.title: Bus write function duplicated 6+ times
redundancies.description: The JSONL atomic-append bus write pattern (os.open O_WRONLY|O_APPEND|O_CREAT, os.write, os.close) is copy-pasted in: coordinator_hub._bus_notify(), help_protocol.HelpProtocol._publish_bus(), direct_channels._bus_publish(), bus_cli.write_msg(), multi_team_runner._bus_write(), and prototype/agent_comm/bus.BusWriter.publish(). All share the same message schema {id, type, channel, team, agent_id, ts, ttl, body} and the same channel-name sanitization logic. This is the single largest source of code duplication across the entire system.

redundancies.title: Bus read function duplicated 3 times
redundancies.description: Bus reading with offset tracking is implemented in direct_channels._bus_read(), bus_cli.read_msgs(), and prototype/agent_comm/bus.BusReader.poll(). Each has slightly different edge-case handling (partial lines, encoding) but the core logic is identical.

redundancies.title: _retry_on_busy decorator duplicated 3 times
redundancies.description: The SQLite BUSY retry decorator is independently defined in coordinator_hub.py, help_protocol.py, and direct_channels.py. All three use the same constants (_MAX_RETRIES=5, _RETRY_BACKOFF=0.1) and the same exponential backoff pattern. help_protocol has a slightly enhanced version that checks sqlite_errorcode, while the other two only do string matching.

redundancies.title: SQLite database initialization duplicated across modules
redundancies.description: Database setup (PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL, PRAGMA busy_timeout, schema creation, os.makedirs) is independently implemented in coordinator_hub._open_db(), help_protocol.__init__(), direct_channels.__init__(), bus_cli.init_db(), and multi_team_runner._get_db()/_init_db(). Each creates connections with the same WAL mode and busy timeout settings.

redundancies.title: Three separate status/progress tracking systems
redundancies.description: There are three independent status-tracking mechanisms: (1) coordinator_hub.agent_status table tracks individual agent status/progress, (2) help_protocol.team_status table tracks team-level status/progress, (3) direct_channels.progress table tracks team phase/progress with bottleneck info. All three store progress_pct, current_task/phase, and last_updated timestamps. They serve overlapping purposes and would confuse any agent trying to report status.

tables.help_protocol: team_status (team, status, progress_pct, current_task, work_items_total, last_updated)
tables.direct_channels: progress (team, phase, progress_pct, items_total, items_done, last_updated)

redundancies.title: Two separate presence/liveness systems
redundancies.description: Agent liveness is tracked in two places: (1) multi_team_runner/bus_cli agents table (agent_id, status, last_heartbeat) with dead-agent detection, (2) direct_channels.presence table (team, status, last_seen) with available/busy/helping/away states. The coordinator_hub.agent_status table also effectively tracks presence via its status field. These serve the same fundamental purpose of knowing who is alive and available.

redundancies.title: Schema duplication between bus_cli and multi_team_runner
redundancies.description: The exact same SQLite schema (agents, rate_limits, rate_limit_config, phase_signals, messages, team_findings, think_tank tables) is defined verbatim in both bus_cli.init_db() and multi_team_runner._SCHEMA. The multi_team_runner adds only one extra table (runner_state). This is a pure copy-paste.

redundancies.title: Channel name sanitization duplicated everywhere
redundancies.description: The pattern channel.replace('/', '_').replace('..', '_') appears in coordinator_hub._bus_notify(), help_protocol._publish_bus(), direct_channels._safe_channel(), bus_cli.write_msg(), multi_team_runner._bus_write(), and both prototype bus modules. A trivial one-liner, but symptomatic of the broader duplication problem.

simplification_opportunities.title: Extract a shared bus_core module
simplification_opportunities.description: Create a single bus_core.py with: Message dataclass, bus_write() function, bus_read() function, channel sanitization, and the _retry_on_busy decorator. All 6+ modules that duplicate this logic can import from one place. This alone would eliminate ~300 lines of duplicated code.

simplification_opportunities.title: Unify status tracking into coordinator_hub only
simplification_opportunities.description: The coordinator_hub's agent_status table is the most complete and well-designed status system. The team_status table in help_protocol and the progress table in direct_channels should be eliminated. Instead, coordinator_hub should be extended with an optional team-level aggregation view. Agents report to one place; the coordinator reads from one place.

simplification_opportunities.title: Merge help_protocol into coordinator_hub
simplification_opportunities.description: help_protocol.py is architecturally a coordinator-level feature (it manages cross-team work assignment). Its work_items and help_requests tables belong in the coordinator's domain. It should be methods on CoordinatorDashboard rather than a standalone class, since the coordinator is the only entity that should mediate cross-team communication (per coordinator_hub's own design philosophy).

simplification_opportunities.title: direct_channels is overengineered
simplification_opportunities.description: direct_channels.py provides IRC-style channel management (create, join, leave, archive, topic channels), presence tracking, and progress broadcasting. For an agent coordination system where agents are ephemeral and the coordinator mediates all cross-agent communication, this is substantial overengineering. The bus already supports channel-based messaging. The SQLite channel registry, read_offsets table, and presence table add complexity without clear value. Direct file-based bus channels already work without registration.

simplification_opportunities.title: dashboard.py queries the wrong database schema
simplification_opportunities.description: dashboard.py queries from the bus_cli/multi_team_runner schema (agents, phase_signals, team_findings, runner_state tables) but the coordinator_hub uses a completely different schema (agent_status, coordinator_instructions). These two systems are architecturally disconnected. The dashboard should be updated to read from coordinator_hub's schema, or the schemas should be unified.
simplification_opportunities.note: Not lines saved but architectural confusion eliminated

simplification_opportunities.title: think_tank.py is self-contained and well-designed but disconnected
simplification_opportunities.description: think_tank.py reads from team_findings (multi_team_runner schema) and JSON output files. It does not interact with coordinator_hub at all. It is a standalone post-processing script that could work as-is, but it represents yet another data path that fragments the system.

simplification_opportunities.title: bus_cli.py mixes concerns
simplification_opportunities.description: bus_cli.py is both a CLI tool and a library (write_msg, read_msgs, register_agent, post_finding are used as functions). It also duplicates the full database schema. It should be split: the reusable functions go into bus_core, and the CLI remains as a thin wrapper.

simplification_opportunities.title: Dead code: messages table in SQLite
simplification_opportunities.description: The 'messages' table in the bus_cli/multi_team_runner schema is never written to or read from by any module. Messages go to JSONL bus files, not SQLite. The table definition is dead schema.

simplification_opportunities.title: Dead code: rate_limits and rate_limit_config tables
simplification_opportunities.description: The rate_limits and rate_limit_config tables in the bus_cli/multi_team_runner schema are only cleaned up by multi_team_runner._run_cleanup() but are never populated by any module. They are dead schema.

paths: JSONL bus files (global channel + topic channels) - used by all modules
coordinator_hub SQLite agent_status table - agents write, coordinator reads
coordinator_hub SQLite coordinator_instructions table - coordinator writes, agents read
help_protocol SQLite tables (work_items, help_requests, team_status) - shared read/write
direct_channels SQLite tables (channels, presence, progress) + per-channel JSONL files
communication_paths.assessment: Five distinct communication paths is excessive. An agent must potentially interact with 3 different SQLite schemas and the JSONL bus to fully participate. The coordinator_hub was designed as the single point of mediation, but help_protocol and direct_channels bypass this by allowing direct agent-to-agent and team-to-team communication.

overhead_per_status_update.description: A single agent status update currently requires: (1) SQLite INSERT OR REPLACE into agent_status with retry logic and threading lock, (2) optional JSONL bus notification to global channel. If the agent also reports team-level status, it additionally needs: (3) SQLite UPSERT into team_status via help_protocol, (4) another bus notification, (5) SQLite UPSERT into progress via direct_channels, (6) another bus notification. That is up to 3 SQLite writes and 3 bus writes for a conceptually single update.
overhead_per_status_update.recommendation: Consolidate to a single SQLite write + single optional bus notification per status update.

unnecessary_intermediaries: direct_channels.channels table acts as a registry for something the filesystem already tracks (JSONL files exist = channel exists)
direct_channels.read_offsets table persists state that BusReader already tracks in memory
coordinator_instructions table is a polling-based message queue when the JSONL bus already provides message delivery

strengths: Messages persist on disk for debugging/replay
SQLite WAL mode handles concurrent access well
weaknesses: JSONL files grow until rotation (up to 1 hour)
BusReader tracks offsets in memory only (lost on restart)

strengths: Event-driven: select() reacts instantly to messages (sub-millisecond latency)
Natural backpressure via FIFO blocking semantics
Data consumed on read (no unbounded growth)
mmap state avoids SQLite overhead for simple key-value lookups
weaknesses: Named pipes are Linux/Unix only (not Windows-compatible)
Spillover files needed when no reader attached - adds complexity
Messages consumed on read (no replay/debugging capability)
FIFO requires reader to be running or messages spill to disk
select() on FIFOs has edge cases (closed writers, EOF handling)

proto_comparison.efficiency_verdict: Proto B is more efficient for real-time coordination (event-driven vs polling, mmap vs SQLite for heartbeats). Proto A is more practical and debuggable (persistent messages, SQLite for complex queries). For the actual use case of CLI agent coordination (not a high-frequency trading system), Proto A's simplicity wins. The latency difference (30s polling vs sub-ms events) does not matter when agents are Claude Code sessions that take seconds to minutes per action.
proto_comparison.can_they_be_unified: Yes, but the value is low. They are deliberate experiments with different architectures. The production system (storage/coordination/) already chose Proto A's JSONL approach. Proto B should remain as a reference implementation for event-driven patterns. No merging needed.

lessons_to_keep.from_proto_a: JSONL bus, SQLite WAL mode, EpochRotator, BusReader offset tracking, Message dataclass
lessons_to_keep.from_proto_b: select()-based event loop pattern (useful if real-time coordination is ever needed), SpilloverCleaner concept, mmap for hot-path state

consolidation_plan.title: Extract bus_core.py
consolidation_plan.description: Create storage/coordination/bus_core.py with: Message dataclass, bus_write(), bus_read(), _sanitize_channel(), _retry_on_busy(). Update all 6+ modules to import from it. This is the highest-ROI change.

consolidation_plan.title: Unify SQLite schema and db_open
consolidation_plan.description: Create a single db_utils.py with open_db() function and the canonical schema. Eliminate the duplicated schema definitions in bus_cli.py and multi_team_runner.py. Merge the bus_cli/runner schema with coordinator_hub schema into one coherent database.

consolidation_plan.title: Consolidate status tracking
consolidation_plan.description: Remove team_status from help_protocol and progress from direct_channels. Extend coordinator_hub.agent_status with optional team-level fields. Update dashboard.py to read from the unified schema.

consolidation_plan.title: Simplify direct_channels
consolidation_plan.description: Remove the SQLite channel registry, presence table, and read_offsets table. Keep only the send_direct/read_direct methods using the bus_core functions. Channels do not need to be registered in SQLite to work.

consolidation_plan.title: Fold help_protocol into coordinator_hub
consolidation_plan.description: Move work_items, help_requests, and team_capabilities tables into coordinator_hub's schema. Add help management methods to CoordinatorDashboard. Remove help_protocol.py as a standalone module. Update bus_cli.py help commands to use coordinator_hub.

consolidation_plan.title: Remove dead schema
consolidation_plan.description: Remove the 'messages', 'rate_limits', and 'rate_limit_config' table definitions that are never used.
